label: Action Tile
title: Action Tile
summary: A compact shortcut to one destination.
corePrinciple: One icon. One short label. One destination.

anatomy.title: One icon, one label, one boundary
anatomy.description: The fixed tile keeps its destination compact. The icon capsule inherits the owner modes supplied to ActionTile.
blocks: Reinforces the destination and receives the owner’s full mode object.
Names one destination with a short, familiar term.
ActionTile owns the fixed 168 × 90 surface and token-driven styling.

anatomy.note: Reinforces the destination and receives the owner’s full mode object.

configuration.title: Pair the label with the right icon
configuration.description: ActionTile exposes the label and icon slot. Keep both focused on the same destination.
blocks: Use a card icon for a card destination.
Change both the label and its icon together.
Keep the destination distinct from neighboring shortcuts.

states.title: Static and actionable are the supported forms
states.description: Supplying onPress makes the tile actionable. The public API does not expose disabled or loading states, so do not invent them.
blocks: Without onPress the tile presents the shortcut information without activation.
With onPress the whole tile activates the named destination.

sizing.title: Keep the public 168 × 90 footprint
sizing.description: ActionTile owns a fixed width and height. Let the surrounding public layout wrap or scroll; do not resize the tile with style patches.
blocks: The tile keeps its intrinsic footprint inside available space.
The host adapts around the tile; the tile itself stays 168 × 90.

content.title: Make every shortcut distinct
content.description: Short nouns usually work best. Avoid duplicate labels or explanatory sentences that turn a shortcut into a card.
blocks: The icon and short label should describe the same place.
Cards, Savings, and Payments are easy to scan in a group.
Each visible tile needs a destination name that distinguishes it from its siblings.

inContext.title: Offer a small set of quick actions
inContext.description: A public HStack owns the responsive group while each fixed tile keeps one destination.

doDont.title: Keep shortcuts concise and unique
doDont.description: The value of a quick-action group comes from immediate recognition.
blocks: Each tile can be understood before it is activated.
Duplicate More tiles do not reveal where either shortcut leads.
Cards is familiar and easy to scan.
Turn the label into a sentence
Long instructions overwhelm a compact shortcut.
The savings icon reinforces the Savings label.
Pair the label with another destination
A cards icon makes the Savings shortcut ambiguous.
specimen: Open the place where you manage all your cards

sources.title: Public component, fixed contract
sources.description: The guide follows the live Figma instance and the package’s public label, icon, modes, and onPress API.
blocks: The public export is jfs-components 0.1.60. Examples use Primary appearance with Medium emphasis, matching the supplied Storybook reference. ActionTile passes those owner modes to its icon capsule.
